briefings.title: Anthropic's Boris Cherny: Why Coding Is Solved, and What Comes Next
briefings.tldr: Coding is effectively "solved" for standard distributions, shifting the developer's role from writing syntax to managing autonomous agent loops.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Coding is effectively "solved" for standard distributions, shifting the developer's role from writing syntax to managing autonomous agent loops. Boris Cherny predicts a democratization of software development on par with the invention of the printing press, where domain expertise replaces technical skill as the primary barrier to entry.

## The Evolution of Claude Code
*   **From Autocomplete to Agents:** Claude Code was built to address "product overhang," where model capabilities exceeded available tools. It transitioned from simple "type-ahead" (tab-complete) functionality to an agentic model that writes 100% of the code.
*   **Model-Driven PMF:** Product-market fit was not immediate; adoption inflected only as model intelligence reached specific thresholds, starting with Opus 4 in May 2025 and accelerating through version 4.7.
*   **Language Distribution:** The model is most effective with "on-distribution" languages like TypeScript and React. While it can now learn new frameworks, Cherny highlights that choosing common languages allowed the model to take over 100% of the codebase earlier.

## The Future of the Developer Workflow
*   **Mobile-First Engineering:** Cherny’s current workflow is largely phone-based, managing dozens of sessions and hundreds of active agents simultaneously via the Claude app.
*   **The Power of Loops:** The "slash loop" command is identified as the most significant workflow shift.
    *   **Automated Maintenance:** Loops use cron jobs to schedule recurring tasks like fixing CI flakiness, auto-rebasing PRs, and clustering user feedback from social media.
    *   **Server-Side Routines:** These allow tasks to persist and execute even when the developer’s laptop is closed.
*   **Extreme Productivity:** Using these autonomous agents, Cherny reports shipping up to 150 PRs in a single day, a feat impossible for manual coding.

## Organizational and Market Disruptions
*   **The Rise of the Cross-Disciplinary Generalist:** Teams are shifting toward "generalists" where every role (Product Managers, Designers, Finance, Research) writes code. Specialist domain knowledge is becoming more valuable than the ability to write syntax.
*   **Eroding Business Moats:** 
    *   **Decreased Moat Value:** "Switching costs" and "process power" (proprietary workflows) are losing value because AI can easily port data and hill-climb complex processes.
    *   **Sustained Moat Value:** Network effects, scale economies, and cornered resources remain critical defenses.
*   **Startup Advantage:** Cherny predicts a 10x increase in startups disrupting incumbents. Small teams can now compete head-to-head with large companies because they lack the "internal resistance" to retraining and evolving legacy business processes.

## Democratization and The "Printing Press" Analogy
*   **Mass Literacy for Software:** Cherny compares the current AI inflection to the 15th-century printing press. Just as the press moved European literacy from 10% to 70%, AI will make software creation a basic life skill similar to sending a text message.
*   **End of the Manual Era:** Anthropic internally claims to have "no more manually written code." All SQL, communications, and scripts are generated by models, with agents communicating with other agents via Slack to resolve technical unknowns.

> "For me today, you know, like the model writes 100% of my code. I write somewhere, you know, usually a few dozen PRs every day. Uh, there was a day last week I did like 150 PRs in a day. That was like, that was a record." — **Boris Cherny**

> "Software will be a thing that is fully democratized, that anyone can do... The best person to write accounting software, I think maybe even today, is not an engineer, it's a really good accountant. Because they know the domain really well and coding is the easy part." — **Boris Cherny**

> "We have no more manually written code anywhere at the company. All of the SQL is written by models. Everything is just built by the models." — **Boris Cherny**

briefings.title: Attention Crisis: How leaders can fix focus and happiness in an AI Era -psychologist Jonathan Haidt
briefings.tldr: Social psychologist Jonathan Haidt warns that social media and AI are dismantling the foundations of human happiness—relational connection, meaningful work, and shared truth—requiring urgent regulatory accountability and a collective return to "effortful" living to prevent the destruction of human capital.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Social psychologist Jonathan Haidt warns that social media and AI are dismantling the foundations of human happiness—relational connection, meaningful work, and shared truth—requiring urgent regulatory accountability and a collective return to "effortful" living to prevent the destruction of human capital.

## The Foundations of Happiness vs. AI
Haidt argues that happiness is not a product of material prosperity or internal mindset alone, but emerges from the quality of relationships "between" ourselves and our world.

*   **The Relational Triad:** True flourishing requires healthy connections between:
    *   **Self and Work:** Finding purpose in productivity and mastery.
    *   **Self and Others:** Strong, supportive human bonds.
    *   **Self and Something Larger:** Coherence within a shared meaning system or truth.
*   **The AI Threat:** AI risks "cracking" these foundations by replacing human effort with shortcuts.
    *   **Meaningless Prosperity:** Universal Basic Income (UBI) may provide money but guarantees "mass meaninglessness" if people lose the drive to be productive.
    *   **Social Erosion:** Chatbots and AI companions may replace human intimacy, preventing the development of essential social and sexual relationship skills.
    *   **Fragmentation:** AI-driven social media has already destroyed shared reality, creating a "fragmentation all the way down" where collective understanding is impossible.

## The Crisis of Human Capital and Childhood
The transition to a "phone-based childhood" between 2010 and 2015 has led to a collapse in mental health and cognitive ability among Gen Z, a trend AI is poised to accelerate.

*   **Developmental Destruction:** Children need to do "hard things" thousands of times to build competence. AI shortcuts—like paper writing and book summarization—threaten to destroy future human flourishing.
*   **The Critical Window:** Haidt suggests we have roughly one year to raise consciousness and implement safeguards before AI integration becomes irreversible.
*   **Accountability Gap:** Tech companies currently operate with zero restraint or liability. Haidt calls for a "you break it, you fix it" regulatory approach, treating social media and AI like any other consumer product with a "death count."
*   **Protecting Puberty:** Brain development during puberty is the most fragile period; addictive algorithms and "engagement loops" have turned children into prisoners of their devices.

## The Attention Crisis in Adults
While the focus is often on the "Anxious Generation" (Gen Z), Haidt notes that adults are suffering from a parallel cognitive decline.

*   **Attention Fragmentation:** The primary locus of damage is the disruption of deep work and cognition. Many adults now report an inability to read a full book or even a paragraph without distraction.
*   **The "Stupidity" Paradox:** As machines get smarter, humans are making themselves "stupider" by outsourcing their thinking and attention to mercenary platforms.
*   **Public vs. Private Interaction:** Moving from face-to-face, private communication to public, algorithmically mediated interactions has been a "disaster for human relationships."

## Restoring Civil Discourse
To combat political polarization, Haidt advocates for moral psychology skills that allow people to communicate across tribal divides.

*   **Constructive Dialogue:** Through the Constructive Dialogue Institute (CDI), Haidt promotes interpersonal skills to navigate "political trench warfare."
*   **Curiosity Over Charity:** Approach disagreements with curiosity. It is not an act of kindness but a tool to become smarter and more effective.
*   **The "Acknowledge" Strategy:** To open a dialogue, start by acknowledging something the other side is correct about. This signals respect and shifts the interaction from "war" to conversation.

## Actionable Strategies for Leaders and Individuals
Haidt emphasizes that "willpower is overmatched" by the behavioral design of modern apps; therefore, environmental change is necessary.

*   **Digital Hygiene:** 
    *   **Device Audits:** List the first five things you do upon waking and the last five before sleeping. If they involve a phone, you are ceding control of your day to the device.
    *   **App Location:** Remove addictive or "slot machine" apps (Instagram, video games, investment sites) from the phone. Access them only via computer to restore intentionality.
*   **Morning Rituals:** Prioritize human or physical contact (touching a person, a pet, or making coffee) before touching a screen to set personal intentions for the day.
*   **Environment Design:** Following the "Grit" philosophy of Angela Duckworth, change your physical environment to change your mental habits.

***

## Notable Quotes

> "AI is saying, 'Hey, take a shortcut. Don't write that paper, don't read that book, I'll summarize it for you.' That is a recipe for the absolute destruction of human capital and the destruction of future human flourishing." — **Jonathan Haidt**

> "Happiness... is actually from between. It's from getting the right relationships between yourself and your work, yourself and others, yourself and something larger than yourself." — **Jonathan Haidt**

> "In the age of AI, as our machines are getting smarter than us very, very quickly, we're helping it along by making ourselves stupider. This does not bode well for the human future." — **Jonathan Haidt**

> "Willpower is overmatched... the apps are designed by people who've studied behaviorism and gambling addiction. You have to do behavioral change: change your environment, and then you can change your thinking." — **Jonathan Haidt**

briefings.title: Digital Freedom, AI Regulation, and the Fight for the Western Internet | The a16z Show
briefings.tldr: The U.S. State Department is shifting its public diplomacy focus from "disinformation curation" to a robust defense of global digital freedom, aiming to ensure the global AI stack possesses a "Western soul" rooted in free expression, user consent, and the rule of law.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The U.S. State Department is shifting its public diplomacy focus from "disinformation curation" to a robust defense of global digital freedom, aiming to ensure the global AI stack possesses a "Western soul" rooted in free expression, user consent, and the rule of law.

## Reforming Public Diplomacy and Digital Freedom
*   **Defining Public Diplomacy:** Under Secretary Sarah Rogers describes her role as managing the relationship between the U.S. government and the foreign public, moving beyond traditional state-to-state diplomacy.
*   **The Shift from Censorship:** Rogers is leading a "truth and reconciliation" effort regarding past government-led censorship (notably the *Murthy v. Missouri* era) where the State Department previously pressured platforms to remove specific content.
*   **New Strategic Priorities:**
    *   **Transparency:** Moving away from "opaque, tyrannical choke points" and toward empowering users with information.
    *   **Circumvention Tools:** Active support for VPNs and censorship-circumvention technologies.
    *   **Decentralized Curation:** Favoring crowd-sourced transparency models, such as X’s Community Notes, over government-funded NGO "fact-checkers."

## AI with a "Western Soul" as Soft Power
*   **The Strategic Stack:** Rogers argues that a Western AI stack is the most significant soft power tool available to the U.S.
    *   **Core Values:** AI models should reason in ways that are individualistic, rules-based, and prioritize user consent.
    *   **National Security:** AI is identified as the next major communications revolution on par with the printing press; securing its development within a Western ideological framework is a top priority.
*   **Protecting Innovation:** 
    *   **IP Security:** Warning against regulations that force companies to disclose model weights, which would allow foreign adversaries to reverse-engineer Western technology.
    *   **Fair Use:** Emphasizing that training AI on publicly available data should be protected under the fair use doctrine to maintain a competitive edge.

## Countering International Regulatory Overreach
*   **The "Censorship Contagion":** Rogers highlights the danger of foreign laws (specifically from the EU and UK) being used to regulate American speech.
    *   **The Thierry Breton Incident:** Cites the European Commission’s attempt to threaten Elon Musk with regulatory penalties before an interview with Donald Trump as a prime example of "viewpoint-skewed enforcement."
    *   **Economic Coercion:** Criticizes the practice of leveraging content-neutral regulations (like algorithm transparency) to punish platforms for hosting protected political speech.
*   **Global Influence:** The administration aims to prevent foreign "petri dishes" of regulation—such as vague "risk assessments" for hate speech—from being imported into American law through lobbying groups.

## Legal Frameworks and Future Governance
*   **Preserving CDA 230 and Fair Use:** Rogers identifies Section 230 and Fair Use as the "bones of the internet" that allowed American tech to thrive; she warns that foreign "strict liability" regimes for AI outputs could dismantle these protections.
*   **Democratic Deliberation vs. Corporate Fiat:**
    *   **Rule of Law:** Argues that critical national security and social questions (e.g., autonomous weapon protocols or data privacy) should be decided in courts and through democratic processes rather than by the "fiat of Silicon Valley executives" or "woke tech workers."
    *   **Viewpoint Neutrality:** Recommends that any future U.S. regulation favor viewpoint neutrality while still allowing platforms to use tools to filter spam, pornography, and foreign provenance content.

> "The proliferation of a Western AI stack should be a top priority for anyone who cares about freedom... AI with a Western soul is the greatest soft power tool we can possess." — **Sarah Rogers**

> "We want to use technology to make people free, rather than institute these kind of opaque, tyrannical choke points far upstream of where the user sees the information." — **Sarah Rogers**

> "When Russia and China censor the internet, they just firewall it off. They don't purport to levy fines on American companies for allowing Americans to engage in First Amendment protected speech on American political issues. The EU did that." — **Sarah Rogers**

briefings.title: Episode 52: Michael Paulus - Founder of PCM Encore
briefings.tldr: Michael Paulus, the serial entrepreneur who bootstrapped Assurance IQ to a $2.35B exit, is now scaling PCM Encore, a multi-family office that applies sophisticated "endowment-style" investment strategies and aggressive tax optimization to high-net-worth individual portfolios.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Michael Paulus, the serial entrepreneur who bootstrapped Assurance IQ to a $2.35B exit, is now scaling PCM Encore, a multi-family office that applies sophisticated "endowment-style" investment strategies and aggressive tax optimization to high-net-worth individual portfolios.

## The Bootstrap Advantage: Building Assurance IQ
*   **Strategic Bootstrapping:** Paulus chose to bootstrap Assurance IQ—an insurtech platform—rather than raising venture capital because the life insurance market provided immediate upfront commissions that supported self-funding.
    *   **Operational Focus:** By avoiding the "distractions" of VC networking and board meetings, the team could remain obsessively focused on customer journey and unit economics.
    *   **Hyper-Metric Tracking:** Without a "safety net" of VC cash, the company tracked performance metrics down to the minute rather than the quarter.
*   **The $2.35B Exit:** The company sold to Prudential Financial in 2019 to solve for capital-intensive Medicare scaling and to gain control over the underwriting process via Prudential’s trillion-dollar balance sheet.

## Transitioning from Venture Capital to Wealth Management
*   **The a16z Experience:** While serving as a Partner at Andreessen Horowitz, Paulus learned he was fundamentally an operator rather than an investor. He noted that great founders must have a "naive belief" in their success, whereas VCs often view opportunities too statistically.
*   **The "Gilded Cage" Risk:** Paulus warns that success often leads to a "gilded cage" where founders are surrounded by "yes-men"; he counters this by staying close to engineers and younger team members.
*   **Genesis of PCM Encore:** After managing his own wealth and his father-in-law’s (Logitech co-founder Daniel Borel), Paulus realized that individual investors lacked access to the sophisticated, tax-efficient "endowment-style" management used by institutions.

## Investment Philosophy: The PCM Encore Strategy
*   **Endowment-Style Portfolios:** The firm focuses on 7–9 non-correlated asset classes to create resilience.
*   **Tax Alpha:** Unlike non-taxable endowments, PCM Encore prioritizes "after-tax" returns for individuals through:
    *   **Direct Indexing:** Maximizing losses to offset gains.
    *   **Real Estate Depreciation:** Utilizing 130–140% depreciation on every dollar invested in specific developments.
*   **Real Estate Thesis:** Paulus targets West Coast multifamily development (specifically in growth hubs like Bellevue) as a bond replacement. 
    *   **Resilience:** He views multifamily as counter-cyclical because people move back into apartments during recessions.
    *   **Rate Play:** Underwriting deals at current interest rates creates "optionality"; if rates drop, mid-teens IRR deals can transform into 40–50% IRR "home runs."

## The Future of Fiduciary Services and AI
*   **AI as a Commodity Driver:** Paulus believes AI will eventually commoditize basic financial planning and public market indexing, which is already a low-cost service.
*   **The Human Edge:** High-value wealth management will shift toward "uncommon investments" (private equity, off-market real estate) and hyper-complex estate planning—areas where AI lacks the necessary private data or human nuance.
*   **Operational Efficiency:** PCM Encore uses AI "under the hood" to increase team efficiency, but delivers the final service with a "human touch."

## Career Wisdom for Young Entrepreneurs
*   **Know Your DNA:** Paulus emphasizes self-awareness—knowing if you are a risk-taking "dreamer" like a VC or a "risk manager" like a banker.
*   **Avoid the Burnout Finish Line:** He admits to facing mental health challenges in his 20s due to self-imposed pressure. His advice is to "enjoy the journey" rather than rushing toward a liquidity event that doesn't inherently bring happiness.
*   **The Power of Mentorship:** He credits much of his success to being mentored by Joe Lonsdale, who exposed him to unique, non-pedestrian business ideas early in his career at Addepar.

> "The most important thing for me in my career is I never want to look at a clock... one of the best gifts, no matter what you do in your life, is that you're excited about the day." — **Michael Paulus**

> "That’s the biggest benefit you get from bootstrapping is just that customer focus—and it's maniacal. If you could go bankrupt this next month, you are really focused on the customer." — **Michael Paulus**

> "A typical endowment-style portfolio is pretty darn inefficient for a taxable investor. We’re always thinking: how do we maximize losses that this client can use either within the portfolio or elsewhere in their life?" — **Michael Paulus**

briefings.title: Howard Marks: AI, Debt vs Equity & The Next 40 Years Of Investing | Nikhil Kamath | People by WTF
briefings.tldr: True investment outperformance requires "second-level thinking" that departs from consensus, as market cycles are driven by emotional excesses rather than predictable mechanical laws.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
True investment outperformance requires "second-level thinking" that departs from consensus, as market cycles are driven by emotional excesses rather than predictable mechanical laws. While artificial intelligence can optimize pattern recognition, exceptional human insight remains essential for navigating unpredictable market shifts, pricing distressed assets, and managing downside risk.

---

## The Philosophy of Preparation and the Mechanics of Cycles

*   **The Concept of Mujo:** Howard Marks attributes much of his foundational perspective to his study of Japanese literature, specifically the concept of *Mujo*—the inevitability of change.
    *   **Inherent Unpredictability:** Because change is inevitable, unpredictable, and uncontrollable, investors must learn to accommodate to it rather than trying to forecast specific outcomes.
*   **Preparation vs. Prediction:** Marks emphasizes that investors should focus on preparation rather than prediction.
    *   **Portfolio Sub-optimization:** Rather than building a portfolio optimized for a single predicted future, investors should build portfolios that can survive multiple potential futures, avoiding extreme vulnerability to negative tail events.
*   **The Psychology of Market Cycles:** Economic cycles do not behave like regular physical waves; they are dictated by human behavior.
    *   **Excesses and Corrections:** Market cycles oscillate around a long-term trend line due to psychological extremes—excessive optimism leads to over-expansion, which inevitably requires a correction down to the mean.
    *   **The Illusion of the Average:** While the S&P 500 has returned an average of 10% annually over the last 100 years, its actual annual return is almost never between 8% and 12%. The market is almost always reacting to excesses of greed or fear.

---

## Debt Investing and Oaktree’s Risk-Controlled Strategy

*   **The Appeal of Contractual Returns:** Despite having capped upside compared to equity, debt investing appealed to Marks's naturally conservative disposition.
    *   **Underpriced Assets:** Oaktree historically targeted fields that the broader market viewed with extreme skepticism, such as high-yield "junk" bonds or distressed debt (rebranded as "opportunistic credit"). 
*   **Calculating the Probability of Default:** The core skill set at Oaktree is predicting default probabilities more accurately than the consensus.
    *   **Excess Returns:** If the market demands a high interest rate based on an assumed 5% default rate, but Oaktree's bottom-up analysis determines the true risk is only 2%, they capture an "excess return."
*   **Institutional Discipline:** Oaktree has maintained a default rate roughly one-third of the market's 3.6% to 3.7% long-term high-yield average through specific structural choices:
    *   **Lifetime Analysts:** Unlike firms where analysts quickly transition to portfolio managers, Oaktree encourages analysts to remain in their roles long-term, building deep institutional knowledge.
    *   **Rigorous Coverage:** Analysts must evaluate eight core areas of inquiry for every company to ensure they do not miss systemic blind spots.

---

## The Limits of AI and the Power of "Second-Level Thinking"

*   **AI's Edge and Boundaries:** AI models excel at analyzing historical data, identifying repeating patterns, and executing strategies with disciplined consistency, free from fear and greed.
    *   **The Novelty Problem:** AI is structurally limited when dealing with situations that have no historical precedent or pattern, such as evaluating unique business plans or identifying exceptional leaders like Steve Jobs.
*   **Second-Level Thinking:** To achieve above-average investment performance, an investor must think differently and *better* than the consensus.
    *   **The Herd Limitation:** If an investor relies on the same consensus data and thinking as everyone else, they will achieve average results. 
    *   **Uncoachable Trait:** Just as you "cannot coach height" in basketball, Marks believes you cannot easily teach the intuitive, non-consensus mindset required for second-level thinking.
*   **The Valuation of Information:** Marks notes that readily available quantitative data about the present cannot yield superior returns because it is already priced into the market. Superior insight relies on interpreting this data differently.

---

## Mindset, Intentionality, and Lifelong Learning

*   **Drifting vs. Intentionality:** Marks describes the first 35 years of his career as being "adrift" on a river of happenstance and luck, which included his transition from equities to bonds in 1978.
    *   **The Entrepreneurial Trigger:** It was not until the founding of Oaktree in 1995 that Marks transitioned to acting with deliberate, proactive intentionality. He suggests that entrepreneurship naturally forces individuals to stop drifting.
*   **Staying Sharp at Eighty:** Marks maintains his cognitive agility through genetic luck, puzzle-solving, reading outside his field, and collaborating with younger professionals—specifically his son, Andrew.
    *   **Intellectual Flexibility:** Despite working in credit for nearly five decades, Marks remains willing to challenge his own assumptions, as demonstrated by his recent deep dives into generative AI models.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "You can't predict, you can prepare. We can't predict the future, we can't control the future, but we can prepare for the future." — Howard Marks

> "Just remember, none of this is easy. Anybody who thinks it's easy is stupid." — Charlie Munger (quoted by Howard Marks)

> "If you think the same as everybody else, you'll act the same as everybody else. If you act the same as everybody else, your investments will perform the same as everybody else. So to perform better you have to deviate from the herd." — Howard Marks

briefings.title: Is a Market Melt-Up Coming? Why Tech & Semis Are Dominating Again | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 58
briefings.tldr: Despite recent geopolitical volatility, market leadership has rapidly reverted to AI, semiconductors, and power-related industrials, suggesting a potential 1999-style "melt-up" rather than a fundamental regime change.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Despite recent geopolitical volatility, market leadership has rapidly reverted to AI, semiconductors, and power-related industrials, suggesting a potential 1999-style "melt-up" rather than a fundamental regime change.

## Market Sentiment and Price Action
*   **Headlines vs. Price Action:** Much like the spring of the previous year, the market recently experienced a brief "swoon" (down 7-9%) only to recover rapidly. Leadership has returned to the same themes: AI, tech, power, and banks.
*   **The "Melt-Up" Thesis:** Chris Verrone suggests the market may be entering a melt-up phase reminiscent of 1999, characterized by narrow leadership and high velocity.
    *   **Symbolic IPOs:** High-profile upcoming IPOs like SpaceX or OpenAI could serve as symbolic markers of a market peak, similar to Blackstone in 2007 or AOL-Time Warner in 1999.
*   **Gold’s Failed Role:** Gold has failed to act as a traditional safe-haven or inflation hedge during the recent Middle East conflict.
    *   **Risk Asset Correlation:** Gold has recently traded more like a tech stock (correlated with the NASDAQ) rather than a defensive asset.
    *   **Extreme Flows:** In January, gold and precious metal ETFs saw "metal mania," with over $100 billion in notional trading in a single day.

## The Semiconductor Takeover vs. Software’s Decline
*   **Semiconductor Concentration:** Semiconductors now represent **17% of the S&P 500**, up from just 2% a decade ago. 
    *   **Industry Evolution:** The group is becoming as dominant as Energy was in the 2000s or Tech in 1999. Micron is now larger than Johnson & Johnson; Nvidia and Broadcom are major index drivers.
*   **Software Neglect:** Software’s weight in the index has dropped from the teens to single digits (approx. 7-8%).
    *   **Indiscriminate Selling:** Software stocks are being sold regardless of performance. For example, ServiceNow reported strong 22% growth but saw its stock drop 14% on the news.
    *   **Generational Oversold Conditions:** Software is deeply "oversold," but Chris Verrone notes that a bottom likely won’t form until semiconductors finally crack.

## Financials and the Credit Landscape
*   **Bank Resilience:** Traditional banks remain strong. Citigroup is currently viewed as a "canary in the coal mine"; its continued strength suggests the market is not yet facing a systemic credit event.
*   **Private Equity (PE) Risks:** Unlike banks, PE firms and alternative asset managers are under pressure due to their heavy exposure to the struggling software sector and private credit.
    *   **Apollo Exception:** Apollo has acted better than peers largely due to its lower exposure to software lending.
*   **Credit Conditions:** While credit spreads have widened slightly since January, they have not "blown out." The lack of deterioration in consumer or commercial credit data suggests a major financial crisis is not imminent.

## Industrials, Power, and Energy
*   **The "Power" Trade:** Industrials associated with the electrical grid and AI infrastructure are thriving.
    *   **GE Vernova (GEV):** This spin-off is now larger than GE Aerospace, highlighting the massive demand for gas turbines (a market controlled by only three global players: GEV, Mitsubishi, and Siemens).
    *   **Other Leaders:** Eaton, Vertiv, and Quanta Services continue to show strength.
*   **Transportation as a Recession Gauge:** Transports (truckers and rails) are reaching all-time highs. This outperformance makes it difficult to maintain a "recession" base case, as transports usually decline ahead of economic downturns.
*   **Energy Outlook:** Energy remains in a long-term uptrend that began in late 2023. Recent corrections are viewed as opportunities to increase exposure rather than exit positions.

## Notable Quotes
> **Chris Verrone:** "The drawdown frankly wasn't deep enough... what was still very much is. The story that we've had for the last year—AI, tech, power, banks—is the same story. This has not been a resetting event."

> **Todd Sohn:** "Semis are 17% of the S&P now... 10 years ago, that number was 2%. We are in a semiconductor world now... your diet is changing. It's becoming more semi-heavy."

> **Chris Verrone:** "Raise your odds of some type of a melt-up here. The shades of the parallels of '99 with this memory [chip] move, the way the leadership has come right back to the same old stocks... raise your odds."

> **Steve Eisman:** "If you annotated every geopolitical event in history [on a chart], you really wouldn't notice. But if you annotated every financial event in history, you certainly would... The war could end tomorrow; the financial event is not ending tomorrow."

briefings.title: LIVE: President Trump participates in a small business summit at the White House — 5/4/2026
briefings.tldr: President Trump hosted the 2026 National Small Business Week Award winners to celebrate the U.S. small business sector’s contribution to the economy and to highlight his administration's "Great Big Beautiful Bill," which focuses on aggressive deregulation, significant tax cuts, and record-breaking capital investment.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Trump hosted the 2026 National Small Business Week Award winners to celebrate the U.S. small business sector’s contribution to the economy and to highlight his administration's "Great Big Beautiful Bill," which focuses on aggressive deregulation, significant tax cuts, and record-breaking capital investment.

## Economic Policy and the "Great Big Beautiful Bill"
* **Capital Investment:** The President reported that $18 trillion has been invested in the U.S. economy over the last 11 months, significantly outpacing the previous administration's four-year total of less than $1 trillion.
* **Tax Reform Highlights:**
    * **Targeted Exemptions:** The administration has passed "no tax on tips," "no tax on overtime," and "no tax on Social Security" for seniors.
    * **Capital Expansion:** Trump highlighted the implementation of 100% expensing and bonus depreciation, allowing businesses to deduct the full cost of new facilities and equipment in the first year rather than over 38 years.
* **Small Business Impact:** 
    * According to the President, 12 million small businesses received an average tax cut of over $7,000.
    * The pass-through deduction is providing an average of $4,600 in savings to 8 million entrepreneurs, projected to generate $750 billion in growth.

## Deregulation and Federal Reform
* **Regulatory Ratios:** The President claimed the administration is currently eliminating 129 old regulations for every one new regulation passed, far exceeding his first-term goals.
* **Labor Market Shifts:** 
    * **Private Sector Growth:** Trump stated that 100% of all new jobs created since his inauguration have been in the private sector.
    * **Federal Workforce Reduction:** The administration has intentionally cut "bloated" federal jobs; Trump argued that former government employees are now earning significantly more in the private sector.
* **Safety and Infrastructure:** The President asserted that Washington D.C. has been transformed into one of the safest cities in the country over the past year.

## Energy, Technology, and Global Trade
* **Energy Outlook:** Joined by Secretary of Energy Chris Wright, Trump noted that oil prices are currently around $100 per barrel and predicted they would drop "substantially" and "rapidly" once current global conflicts subside.
* **Artificial Intelligence:** Trump emphasized the importance of the U.S. leading China in AI development, noting that new AI and auto plants are being constructed across the country.
* **Trade and Tariffs:** The President defended the use of tariffs to protect domestic businesses from "inferior" products from China and other nations, suggesting that tariffs incentivize foreign companies to build plants within the U.S.

## National Security and Governance
* **Iran and Nuclear Proliferation:** Trump touched upon a recent "military operation" regarding Iran, stating that the U.S. "can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon." He claimed the operation has severely degraded Iran’s military capabilities.
* **Cognitive Fitness:** The President spent a significant portion of his remarks advocating for cognitive tests for all presidential and vice-presidential candidates. 
    * **Personal Record:** Trump stated he has "aced" three separate cognitive tests administered by doctors, including Ronnie Jackson.
    * **Proposed Standards:** He suggested that while some find it "unconstitutional," a cognitive test is necessary to ensure leaders have "what it takes" for the role.

## Notable Quotes
> "As small business owners and operators, the people in this room represent the 36 million small businesses and create 40% of all economic activity in the United States... you’re essentially the most important factor business-wise in the whole country." — **President Donald J. Trump**

> "We virtually eliminated the unfair estate tax or death tax for farmers and for small businesses... if you do like to leave [your business] to somebody that you love, then it’s a big deal for them." — **President Donald J. Trump**

> "We are getting rid of 129 nonsense regulations for every new one that we pass... factory construction is way up. Consumer confidence is way up. Business investment is more than triple compared to that of just a short time ago." — **President Donald J. Trump**

> "In 11 months, $18 trillion investments. We have auto plants being built all over the country, AI plants, we’re doing, and we’re leading China in AI." — **President Donald J. Trump**

briefings.title: Stanford Leadership Forum 2026: Conversation with Ken Griffin
briefings.tldr: Leadership in a volatile, AI-driven era requires a relentless commitment to meritocracy, the agility to abandon "sunk costs" immediately, and a focus on lifelong learning to stay ahead of rapid technological shifts that are eroding traditional competitive moats.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Leadership in a volatile, AI-driven era requires a relentless commitment to meritocracy, the agility to abandon "sunk costs" immediately, and a focus on lifelong learning to stay ahead of rapid technological shifts that are eroding traditional competitive moats.

## Leadership and Decision-Making Under Uncertainty
* **The "Sunk Cost" Fallacy:** Successful organizations avoid the trap of sticking to a failing direction to save face.
    * At Citadel, the culture focuses on admitting mistakes quickly ("Ah, we screwed that up, next") rather than burying them in paperwork, a common failure in large global banks.
    * **Flexibility as a Competitive Edge:** Leaders must be willing to "snap the neck" of an organization by changing direction the moment information shifts.
* **Resilience in Crisis:** Griffin describes the 2008 financial crisis as a "near-death experience" for Citadel rather than an academic exercise.
    * **Key Lesson:** The crisis revealed the danger of non-bank institutions relying on wholesale funding markets that can vanish instantly. The primary takeaway was "don't pretend to be a bank unless you are a bank."
* **Learning from Failure:** History is written by winners, but Griffin emphasizes studying the chapters where things went off the rails, citing Steve Jobs' failures (like the Apple Newton) as essential components of eventual success.

## Market Integrity vs. Crony Capitalism
* **Crony Capitalism vs. Merit:** Griffin argues that favoritism and "state capitalism" lead to inferior products and lower standards of living.
    * **Merit-Based Success:** American prosperity is driven by first-generation entrepreneurs (Bezos, Zuckerberg, Huang) who built trillion-dollar businesses from nothing, the antithesis of an oligarchic society.
* **The Executive Voice:** Corporate leaders should speak publicly on issues where they have credible expertise—such as immigration, tariffs, and antitrust—but should generally stay out of social issues to avoid alienating the public.
* **Healthy Competition:** Griffin views underperformance (e.g., losing to competitors over a six-week period) as a vital catalyst for continuous improvement and internal reflection.

## The AI Revolution and the Erosion of "Moats"
* **"Agentic AI" and High-Skill Jobs:** AI is no longer just providing a 20% boost to software engineers; it is now performing work previously reserved for PhDs and Masters-level researchers in hours rather than months.
    * Griffin notes this shift is "unsettling" because it targets high-level research and white-collar productivity rather than just entry-level tasks.
* **Erosion of Competitive Moats:** Traditional barriers to entry, such as massive data centers or distribution networks, are being neutralized by cloud computing and AI.
    * **Entrepreneurial Opportunity:** It is easier than ever for small startups to challenge incumbents.
    * **Example:** A pet insurance startup recently sold for $1 billion after using AI image generation to identify dog breeds from social media posts and deliver personalized marketing to new owners.
* **Human Capital:** In an AI world, the primary goal of education must be "learning how to learn," as specific technical bodies of knowledge will depreciate faster than ever.

## Education and the Future of the American Dream
* **The Crisis in K-12 Education:** Griffin expressed deep concern over the state of U.S. public schools, noting that in some districts, not a single student is proficient at grade level in math.
* **Historical Illiteracy:** He argues that a functioning democracy requires a populace that understands its history. He cites a lack of understanding regarding the failures of socialism as a threat to the "last beachhead" of personal liberty.
* **Giving Back:** Griffin emphasizes an "intergenerational spirit of giving," where successful leaders have a high expectation to contribute time and resources to their communities and mentor the next generation.

## Career Advice for Future Leaders
* **Surround Yourself with "Non-Clones":** Effective leaders do not hire people like themselves. They seek diverse perspectives (different backgrounds and life experiences) to create the tension and debate necessary for better decision-making.
* **Passion vs. Wealth:** Pursuing wealth for the sake of wealth leads to disappointment. 
    * Greatness requires a combination of talent and intrinsic motivation. 
    * Griffin encourages graduates to find work that resonates "deep in their soul," as that durability is required to survive the "roller coaster" of high-stakes leadership.

> "The biggest difference between Citadel and [large global banks]... there’s no sunk cost here. Where I worked, everyone would try to figure out who to blame for the mistake and how to bury it. Here, it’s just like, 'Ah, we screwed that up, next.'" — Ken Griffin

> "The issue here with AI is that in the world of AI, humans were the horses." — Ken Griffin (citing Niall Ferguson)

> "In life you will only be great if you’re both talented and passionate. If you think you’re going to pursue just wealth for the sake of wealth, you’ll be profoundly disappointed... find what resonates with you deep in your soul." — Ken Griffin
